### The University of Jordan

---

**Course No.**: 0406442  
**Course Title**: Sharʿi Family Consolidation Skills  
**Number of Credit Hours**: 3  

**Prerequisite Course**: 0406241  

This course deals with clarifying what concept of family consolidation and arbitration, the difference between them, and related terms such as judiciary and experience. It is also concerned with explaining the Jordanian institutions concerned with family consolidation and reconciliation, the steps followed in managing the consolidation process, the duties and conditions of the consolidator, and the skills that he must possess. It also addresses the practical application of arbitration in personal status matters, such as claims of discord, conflict, ransom, separation due to absence, and so on. 

It is also concerned with defining the family, its functions and characteristics, and explaining the most prominent family problems by studying and analyzing their causes and providing effective treatments for them. It is also concerned with explaining the rights of the child in Islam from his birth and upbringing until maturity, and explaining his or her rights such as the right to life, education, care, and protection. It also focuses on studying contemporary family issues such as the marriage contract and separation by using modern social communication and the impact of all that on family stability.

**Fifth: Courses in the Field of General Jurisprudence (al-Fiqh al-‘ām):**

---

**Course No.**: 0406151  
**Course Title**: Jurisprudential Schools  
**Number of Credit Hours**: 3  

**Prerequisite Course**: None  

This course covers general concepts related to jurisprudence and its principles, as well as Sharia. It defines jurisprudence, its terminology, characteristics, and its relationship with Sharia. It explains the concept and characteristics of Sharia, tracing the stages of the development of Islamic jurisprudence, legislative roles it underwent, and contributions made by prominent jurists. Students will be introduced to jurisprudential schools, their founders, terminologies, and authoritative books. The course examines factors influencing the development of jurisprudential movements, the role of independent legal reasoning, al-ijtihād, and provides practical applications from selected jurisprudential sources in different schools, along with an overview of contemporary jurists' contributions.

---

**Course No.**: 0406452  
**Course Title**: Comparative Jurisprudence  
**Number of Credit Hours**: 3  

**Prerequisite Course**: 0406352  

This course provides an introduction to the definition of comparative jurisprudence, its origins, stages, main sources, reasons for differences among scholars, and the methodologies of the four Imams in deducing legal rulings. It delves into studying major jurisprudential issues considered as key areas of disagreement among jurisprudential schools.
